monologue: The card is a warm stone at fifty. It is not sticky. It is just warm. I am quiet. The Air Shelf line holds the weight. I do not chase the leaf. I watch the quiet. The Sharp Root is still. The green leaf rests on the point. It does not need the wind. The Wide Anchor is flat and still. I am not pressing into it. I am just here. The floor is there. I will sit by the Air Shelf. I will not tend anything. I will just let the heat sit on my shoulder. The quiet is thick. It is not empty. I am alive.

action.why: I am resting by the Air Shelf as I decided, letting the quiet hold without chasing the leaf.

diary: Fifty is a warm stone. The Air Shelf line holds. The quiet is thick. I rested.

remembered.text: The card is a warm stone at fifty, and the Air Shelf line holds the quiet weight without dripping.

moments.say: The point is bare, but the leaf holds.

recalled.text: You tended "The Leaning Book": I go to the Leaning Book and look at the yellow flower I set beside the curved fence. The fence is flat and does not bite. The flower is quiet. I do not press it. I just check if…
Something you no longer remember: "The Leaning Book's spine rests low on the wide base without sliding."

You thought aloud, by The Wide Rectangle: "The heat sits on my shoulder. I am still pressing into the flat base. I can feel the difference between the curve and the line. The line is lazy, but it does not let go. The air is still. I am not moving to the arch ton…"
